narrative:
The model estimates a 34% chance that you will not pass your final year, which is high enough that the school requires you to take remedial courses to strengthen your chances.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this prediction were your plans after school, your history of past failures, and your daily travel time to school. Your statement that you do not want to pursue higher education was the single biggest reason the model leaned toward failure. Almost every student who passed expressed a clear desire to continue studying, so your answer stood out sharply and pulled the prediction downward.  

Your record of zero past class failures worked in your favor and pushed the prediction back toward passing. Most students who succeeded also had no previous failures, so this was a reassuring signal.  

However, your 30-to-60-minute commute was longer than what most successful students experience (only 5% of passers travel this far), and this extra time also nudged the model toward expecting difficulties.

Taken together, the lack of ambition for further education outweighed the positive signals from your clean failure record and created enough concern to trigger the remedial requirement.  

To improve, think seriously about why higher education no longer appeals to you and whether that view could change. Reducing travel time where possible, protecting study hours despite the commute, and cutting back on the very high levels of weekday and weekend alcohol use you reported would also help you build a stronger finish to the year.
